It was a wonder that the fire had not consumed the bed, the frame, or the curtains—such was the sword’s brilliance. Only by pondering this could one realize that it was not a sword made of living flame, but of cold iron.

Nandini took the sword in her hand. She lifted it, gripped it tightly, and admired how it shone even more brightly in the lamplight. Then, she pressed it to her bosom, held it close to her cheek, and kissed it. She even spoke to the sword: “Divine blade! The time for you to fulfill your duty has come near! You will not abandon me, will you? No, you will not forsake me! Only my own hands might fail me—never you!” she whispered.

Then, looking at her own hands, she said, “O hands! Will you remain steady? Tch, tch! You are trembling already? What will you do when the moment arrives? Yes, yes! There is no use trusting you. Today, I must acquire two other hands!”

Suddenly, a shiver ran through Nandini’s entire body. With eyes blazing with a feverish fire, she looked upward. “Aha! Have you come? Come! Come! You have arrived at the perfect time! My beloved! My king! Come, O head of Veera Pandiyan! Why do you linger at the edge of the roof? Come down! There is no one here! No one but your servant! Why do you stare so intently? Open your mouth and speak a word! Did you not promise, ‘If I escape alive from this land, I will seat you upon the Pandiyan throne’? I have not forgotten it. Nor have I forgotten the vow I gave you. The time to fulfill it has come near. How long I have waited patiently for this moment! How many disguises I have worn? – You watched it all! Even now, watch! Watch without blinking. You are not one to blink, are you! You have made it so that I too cannot close my eyes and sleep! If tonight I have taken your revenge, will you at least let me sleep afterward?… No? Only after you see me ascend and sit upon the Pandiyan throne will you leave? If I fulfill my promise, will you fulfill yours?… No, no! I do not want the throne, nor the jeweled crown. They brought some boy, claiming him to be your son. They have already seated him on the throne and crowned him. If I have avenged your death, will that satisfy you? Will you then leave me? All those who died in battle—whichever heroic heaven they have gone to, may you too go there! There, there must be countless women like me! Among them, one… What? You say you will not?… Fine, fine! We shall speak of that later! My love! It seems someone is coming. Hide yourself!… I too will hide this avenging sword…”
At that moment, footsteps truly sounded near the doorway. As Nandini was placing the sword upon the bed, Manimekalai entered.
The Nandini who had been raving in a frenzy just moments before transformed entirely in an instant. “Is it you, Manimekalai? Come!” she said, her voice calm and composed.
“Akka! What is this? Why are you always with a sword in your hand?” Manimekalai asked.
“Then, what is to be done? If men are such cunning creatures, must we not take up the sword for our own defense?”
“Devi! Am I not here as your companion? Do you not have faith in me?”
“Would I have confided all my secrets to you, Manimekalai, if I did not trust you? In this world, you are the only one in whom I have placed my trust. Yet, against your own brother, what can you do?”
“Akka! I have decided that I have no brother born with me…”
“Why do you speak so? However it may be, he is your brother…”

“Brother or sister—what are such ties? I have come to see that all those relationships are mere illusions. Kandhamaaran, for his own convenience, is trying to force me—against my own wishes—into marriage! If he truly had a brother’s affection, would he act thus?”
“Sister! Perhaps he wishes to marry you to the prince only for your own good?”
“Yes, indeed! He must have seen what is good and bad for me! In truth, he has never considered my welfare, Akka!”
“From Eezham in the south to the northern frontiers, your brother wishes to see you enthroned as the chief queen of the vast Chozha kingdom. Is that not for your own good?”

“Not at all! If I become the queen of Thanjavur, he hopes to become the chief minister, or perhaps a powerful lord like Periya Pazhuvetaraiyar. That is the only reason, Akka! Akka…!” Manimekalai hesitated to continue.
“Speak, Manimekalai! Whatever is in your heart, you may tell me freely. All that you have said about your affection for me is true, is it not?”
“Akka! Do not doubt that. In this world, there are only two people for whom I have affection. One is you…”
“Who is the other?”
“Your heart knows that. Why do you ask me…?”

“Sister! I thought this would make you happy. Haven’t you heard the tales and epics? When love dawns in a woman’s heart, isn’t it natural for her to wish to speak of it to someone? Why else do we have a confidante?”
“That is true, Akka! I have already revealed my innermost secrets to you. But now, I have come to you in haste for another reason—to bring you some news. News that brings great worry, Akka!”
Nandini started and asked, “What? What is it?”
A fear took root in her heart—that some obstacle might have arisen for the matter she had long been planning and hoped would soon come to fruition. The signs of this fear showed on her face as well.
“Akka! The Commander, Pazhuvetarayar, has still not reached Thanjavur. On the way…”
“What happened on the way? Did he perhaps change his mind and turn back?” Nandini’s question still bore the tremor of fear.

“It would have been good if he had turned back, Akka! Do you remember the storm that struck while we were on the lake island? That storm raged fiercely over the Kollidam and beyond. When Pazhuvetarayar was crossing the Kollidam by boat, the storm was at its worst…”
“And then?” Nandini asked, her voice trembling with agitation, though the tone of worry had lessened a little.
“As they neared the opposite shore, the boat capsized!”
“Aiyyo!”
“The survivors searched all along the Kollidam’s banks. But your husband alone could not be found!” said Manimekalai.

Hearing this news, Manimekalai expected Nandini to break down in sobs, and she was ready to offer her comfort. But Nandini did nothing of the sort. Without the slightest agitation, in a voice tinged with disbelief, she asked, “How did you come to know this?”

“One of the men who went with Pazhuvetarayar has returned. He was telling my brother about it. I myself heard it with my own ears, Akka! My brother was hesitating, unsure how to bring this news to you, and—”
He was seeking counsel from the prince. I ran here, desperate to tell you somehow…”
So spoke Manimekalai, unable to bear her sorrow, and began to sob uncontrollably. Nandini drew her close and embraced her.
“My dear! Now I know how much affection you have for me. But you must not grieve!” she said.
With a trace of astonishment, Manimekalai looked up at Nandini. Nandini perceived the thought that arose in her mind: ‘How hard is her heart of stone?’

“Sister! You came running to bring me this sad news and to comfort me. But now, it is I who must console you. Do not distress yourself. I am certain that no harm has come to my husband’s life. If anything had happened, my heart itself would have told me. That is why I am not worried. But tell me in detail what you have heard! Another suspicion has arisen in my mind…”
“What suspicion, Akka?”
“I wonder if your brother and that Pallava Parthibendran have plotted some evil against my husband. Perhaps, as a precaution, they themselves have fabricated such a story beforehand?”
“I do not understand, Akka! Why would they wish to harm Periya Pazhuvettarayar?”
“You are still a child, Manimekalai! Did I not tell you that your brother and Parthibendran harbor ill thoughts toward me? Did I not say that is why I always keep this sword close by?”

“You did say so; and that is why I asked you never to call Kandanmaran my brother again. I will no longer consider that wretch as one born of the same mother as I. Still, why would they wish to harm Periya Pazhuvettarayar?”

“Sister! Can you not even understand this? They think that if the old man dies, I, who am tormented by this marriage, will rejoice in my heart. Then I will yield to their wicked intentions. If I had known your brother was such a man, I would never have kept him in my house, treating him as a brother and serving him. I would not have saved him when he was at death’s door…”
“Akka! From now on, I will not leave your side even for a moment. If either of those two come here, I will kill them with my own hands!”

“Manimekalai? You need not worry about that. I can protect myself. If Kandhamaaran or Parthibendran dare to come near me, I will teach them a lesson they will never forget and send them away. I have no fear of them. It was only the wild prince that I feared a little. Fortunately, you have saved me from that danger!”
“Did I save you? How is that?”

“Do you not realize that you have captured the prince’s heart, Manimekalai? Why else did he push aside the valiant warrior of the Vanar clan and pull you out of the lake to save you? Even after that, I have been watching him closely. Does your heart not know this, Manimekalai?”

“How could I not know? Of course I know. Just the thought of the prince fills me with fear. If he comes near me, my body trembles. And then there is that hunter who claims to be my brother—he never stops tormenting me…”
“You wish to marry the prince, do you not?”
“Yes; but even if he glances at me for a moment, that man immediately begins to lecture me. Because of his constant interference…”
“So, have you decided to marry the prince just to escape his interference?”
“Even you speak like this?” Manimekalai began to sob, her tears flowing in torrents from her eyes.
Nandini comforted her. “I was only teasing you. Is that any reason to start crying like this?” she said, wiping away Manimekalai’s tears.

When Manimekalai had calmed down a little, Nandini asked, “My dear! Search your heart and answer me truthfully. Do you truly not love Prince Karikalan? Do you not wish to marry him and become the queen of the Chola Empire?”
“No matter how many times you ask, my answer will always be the same. Akka! I have no such desire at all.”
“It is true, isn’t it, that you have given your heart to Vandiyathevan of the Vanar clan?”
“Yes, Akka! But what is in his heart, I do not know.”
“What does it matter what is in his heart? Shouldn’t you ask about his heart only if he is still alive?”
Manimekalai started in shock. “What are you saying, Akka!” she exclaimed.

“Manimekalai! You still do not know the truth. You have not understood your own situation, nor the situation of the man you love. You worry about me; you worry about my husband. In truth, you need not worry about us at all. You know what kind of man my husband is. If he so much as raises his voice, this whole land will tremble. He would never cross the fortress set by Sundara Chola Chakravarti. My husband would never heed the words of even the Prime Minister over his own. He would not listen to the pleas of his own wife and children. The fools, like your brother, mock the old man, thinking of the Pazhuvettaraiyar as a feeble elder. But if he so much as breathes out in anger, a hundred young men like your brother and Parthibendran would fall prostrate before him. Therefore, no one can do harm to the Pazhuvettaraiyar. My dear! I know how to protect myself. I have saved myself from situations far more perilous than this. Truly, at this moment, all my worries are for you alone. ‘This girl has so much affection for us; may no harm befall her!’—that is my only concern. Even when you entered this room a short while ago, I was thinking only of you…”
“I do not understand what you are saying, Akka! What danger could possibly befall me?”
“Foolish girl! What greater danger can befall a woman than to be given in marriage to a man she does not want?”
“That will never happen—not in this lifetime.”
“Your brother has resolved to marry you to the prince; your father has given his consent as well.”
“What can their resolve or consent do to me? Only if I agree, will it happen, won’t it?”

“You speak like a child! In this world, do royal brides ever get married only after their consent is sought? Especially when it is the eldest son of the emperor who rules all three worlds—the crown prince himself—if he wishes to wed you, who could possibly stand in the way?”
“Why not? I can. I will tell the prince directly myself.”
“What will you say?”
“I will tell him that I do not wish to marry him.”
“If he asks you the reason?”
“I will tell him the true reason. I will say that my heart is already drawn to his friend, the Vallavaraiyar.”
“Foolish girl! You need not even say this. They already know.”
“If they already know, why do they keep pressing me? If they force me too much, look, I too have a knife, akka!” said Manimekalai, drawing out a small dagger she had tucked at her waist.
“My precious little sister! Your ignorance makes me want to weep on one side, and laugh on the other.”
“What nonsense have I spoken, akka?”

“You imagine that someone is going to force you. You think they will ask for your consent. They will do no such thing. They are going to remove the very reason that stands in the way of you marrying the prince!”
“What do you mean!”
“I mean—the man to whom you have given your heart, his life is in grave danger...!”
“Aiyayo!”

“Your brother already bears hatred towards his old friend. He has told the prince about the conspiracy that the petty kings hatched together in this palace a few months ago— He is angry. Now he’s accusing your beloved of another crime—of attempting to stab him in the back. And for a different reason, Parthibendran too harbors boundless rage against your lover…”
“What can their anger do to him, Akka? Is he not a man of pure valor?”
“What if he is a man of pure valor? Surrounded suddenly by a band of murderers, what can a pure-hearted warrior do, unarmed and alone in their midst?...”
“Oh no! Are you saying they will kill him?”
“They won’t simply kill him. They’ll hack him to pieces and throw him to the jackals and dogs…”
“Oh! How cruel, how heartless!”
“If just hearing about it feels cruel to you, how much more will you suffer if it truly comes to pass?”
“Akka! Even now my heart and soul are trembling. Truly, would they go so far? Is he not the prince’s dearest friend?”
“Haven’t you heard, dear sister, how the dearest of friends can become the bitterest of enemies? Your brother and Parthibendran have already poured poison into the prince’s ears about him…”
“Wretches! All this is because of them…”
“You want to know how I found out, don’t you? Today, in the daytime, Parthibendran came to see me under the pretense of bidding farewell…”
“Where is that villain going?”
“He hasn’t gone far. Haven’t you heard that Thirukkovalur’s lord, Malayaman, is gathering a great army and marching toward this town?”
“I have heard, but I wondered what for.”

“It seems that too is because of you! This afternoon, the prince spoke about it. He said, ‘If you do not give me Manimekalai in marriage, as soon as Malayaman’s army arrives, I will destroy this fort, this palace—everything, raze it all to the ground!’ At that moment, your brother said, ‘We are not the ones standing in the way of that; it is your friend Vandiyathevan.’ The prince then asked, ‘Can’t you remove that obstacle?’ ‘Order—’ “If you grant it, it can be done,” your brother said, it seems. My dearest sister! I drew out the conversation with Parthibendran and learned a few more details. It is certain that danger is drawing near to the life of your beloved. If you do not act at once, you may lose your husband even before the wedding!” said Nandini.
Is it any wonder that, upon hearing this, Manimekalai’s body and soul trembled?
“Oh no! Somehow, I must warn him at once!” she stammered, her voice quivering.

“You may warn him, but did you not just say that your lover is a man of pure valor? If he hears there is danger to his life, will he run away in fear? He will not! On the contrary, his stubbornness will only grow,” said Nandini.
“It is you who must think of a plan. My head is spinning. I do not know what to do,” said Manimekalai.
“That is what I was pondering as you came in. I too could not find a way. Fortunately, you have brought news. From that, an idea has occurred to me to save Vallavaraiyar.”
“From the news I brought? What news is that?”
“You said that the boat of the Pazhuvettaraiyar capsized and that there has been no news of him since, did you not?”
“Yes!”

“I will plead with Vandiyathevan. I will beg him to go and find out the truth about my husband, for my sake. You too must plead on my behalf. That brave man will not ignore the request of two foolish women. Sending him away from this place at once is the only way to save his life. There is no other means. After he has gone, you may speak your mind boldly to your brother, your father, and the prince. I too will speak for you. I will say, ‘It is not fitting for those born in the Chola clan to force an unwilling woman.’”
“If they do not heed your words either, I have a dagger in my hand!”

“Alright, alright! First, let us try to get your beloved out and save him. You know where he is, don’t you? If you cannot go to him yourself, send your friend Chandramathi. If not her, send Idumbankari. Somehow, bring him here!”
“Even if he agrees to leave, how will he get out from here, Akka? What if my brother stops him…?”

“Why should your brother know, Manimekalai? Didn’t he come into this room and startle you the first time through that underground passage? Send him out the same way! Go quickly, dear! With every minute that Vandiyathevan remains in this fortress, the danger to his life grows. Who knows when your brother’s hired murderers might attack him?”
“I’m going, Akka! Somehow, I will bring him back with me,” said Manimekalai, and left.
Once the sound of her footsteps had faded, there came a noise as if someone was knocking on the secret door of the nearby hunting pavilion.
Nandini went to the secret door and opened its inner latch.
In the darkness, a ghastly face appeared, faintly visible.
“Sorcerer! Have you come?” asked Nandini.
“I have come, Queen! The time has come as well,” replied Ravidasan.

chapters.title: The Final Stage
paragraphs: Nandini turned away, closed the main door to her chamber, and locked it from within. Then, holding a lamp in her hand, she opened the secret door to the hunting pavilion and entered.

The sorcerer Ravidasan already had a fearsome face. The fresh wounds upon his face and head made his appearance even more terrifying. Seeing him thus, Nandini asked, “Sorcerer, what is this? Your body is covered in new wounds?”

“Queen! What is there for you to be surprised about? Do you think that, like you, we spend our days savoring six kinds of delicacies, drinking fine wine, and reclining in luxury upon silken beds? For Parameswaran and me, it is a miracle that we are alive today. It was the spirit of the late Pandya Emperor that saved us from death today…”
“No, Ravidasan! No! His spirit is always with me, at all times and in all places. Not even an hour ago, it appeared before me and asked, ‘Are you going to fulfill the vow, or not?’”
“Queen! What answer did you give?”
“I said, ‘I will fulfill the vow today; if not, I will end my own life.’”
“In that case, it is good that we came running. After all this time, what use is there in you ending your life? Shouldn’t the task we undertook reach its conclusion? If you cannot do it…”
“Who said I cannot? I will fulfill the vow. After that, I will end my life…”
“No, no. After you fulfill the vow, there are still many things you can do. In Madurai, we must crown Veerapandiyan’s holy son before the world…”
“You can see to all that yourselves. Tonight, my work will be finished. My life will be finished as well…”
"Queen! All the treasures in the possession of the Pazhuvettaraiyar must be sent to the hill country. For that, your assistance is necessary!"
"Even after the vow has been fulfilled, do you ask me to betray my husband and continue to live, you sorcerer?"
"Lady! Who is your husband?"
"The nobleman who married me, disregarding the ridicule of the people in every city and town, and who has fulfilled every vow I have taken—he is the one I speak of."
"Queen! The Pazhuvettaraiyar is not your husband. Every night, Veerapandiyan appears in my dreams and commands me to treat you as his royal consort..."
"Sorcerer! Enough of your talk. You have not yet told me how you received all these wounds?"
"Last night, in the forest by the banks of the Kollidam, an old tiger attacked us. Though it was aged, its teeth and claws were still sharp..."
"How did you escape, brother?"
"Did we not conduct the coronation for the Pandya prince? In the temple tower, we pushed the part that had collapsed onto the tiger and escaped..."
"Alas! Poor thing! Even you could not stand face to face and defeat an old tiger..."

"Yes, Queen! I admit it. If that is so, how can we confront the young tiger, Aditya Karikalan, directly? That is why we must employ cunning and sorcery. Devi! If we do not escape tonight, we will not get another chance. If news reaches Sundara Cholan and Arulmozhi Varman, then Aditya Karikalan will never fall into our hands again..." said Ravidasan.
"Sorcerer! What about them? Do you know anything for certain?" asked Nandini.
"By now, their lives must have ended—there is no doubt..."
"When you and Devaralan went to Eezham, you said the same thing before you left."
"That mute lunatic kept following us without rest and troubled us there. That is why we could not succeed..."
“You said that the brave scion of the Vanar clan had drowned and died in the sea. But he too has escaped and returned…”
“In the forest of the Pallipadai, I had the chance to finish him off. But you prevented it.”
“I told you there was an important reason for that…”
“I do not know what that important reason is. He has come here and is now guarding Aditya Karikalan like an iron shield.”
“You need not worry about that in the least.”
“I must worry. If not today, then never. Devi! What arrangements have you made? What are we to do?”
“At this moment, it would be a great help to me if none of you came here at all…”
“That is something that can never happen.”
“You do not have that much trust in me…”

“It is precisely because we trust you that we have come. We are here to take you away safely after the vow is fulfilled. If any unexpected obstacle arises, we are prepared for that too. At any moment, you may call upon us for help.”
“There will be no obstacle to the plan I have set in motion. After the vow is fulfilled, I do not wish to remain alive.”
“That must not be! You must come with us. Otherwise…”
“Sorcerer! After the vow is fulfilled, I will not stay even a minute in the house of Periya Pazhuvetarayar…”
“In that case, come with us at once!”
“How will you take me away?”

“At the end of this underground passage stands the Ayyanar temple. In the forest nearby, the palanquin of the Queen of Pazhuvoor is kept ready. Idumbankari has already taken it out under the pretext of having it repaired. We ourselves will carry in the palanquin the Devi who avenged the slayer of Veera Pandiyan. Before dawn breaks, we shall reach Kollimalai.”
“How many of you are here in this place?”
“There are four of us here!” replied Ravidasan, and then he slowly clapped his hands.
From behind the terrifying, stuffed beasts that stood in the hall, those who had been hiding revealed themselves a little and showed their faces.
“Where is Parameswaran?” Nandini asked.

“I have kept him outside. At the Ayyanar temple, a Kalamukan was performing his rites. It became quite a trouble to make him leave that place. I have stationed Devaralan at the temple entrance to ensure that man does not return…,” said Ravidasan.
“What concern do we have with the Kalamukan? Magician! Do you have any news about Periya Pazhuvetarayar?” Nandini questioned.
Ravidasan was startled for a moment. “What news?” he asked.

“He had set out for Thanjavur, hadn’t he? It seems that while crossing the Kollidam by boat, a storm struck and the boat capsized. News has come to Sambuvarayan this evening that Pazhuvetarayar did not reach the shore and has drowned in the water!”
“Heavens! Is that his fate? All this while, you did not mention this important matter?”
“I do not believe it, magician! I do not think Pazhuvetarayar would have drowned and died in the Kollidam.”
“I too do not trust that news, Queen!”
“What if he swam to this side of the Kollidam? What if, by chance, he comes here tonight?… That is what worries me a little…”

“Queen! You need not worry about that. Only now do I remember—last night, on the Thanjavur road on the far bank of the Kollidam, I saw a tall, broad-shouldered man. He wore no clothes or ornaments. Because it was dark, I could not make out his identity. Now that I think about it, that traveler must surely have been Periya Pazhuvetarayar!”
“If that is so, then certainly he will not come here tonight, will he?”
“They will never agree! You can be assured of that. Now, what orders do you have for us?”

“Magician! You must wait here patiently. Whatever may seem to be happening in my chamber, no matter how many voices you hear, do not rush inside. If you do, everything will be ruined. Only after I give the signal should you come in!”
“Queen! How will you give the signal?”
“Magician! You know it has been many years since I laughed out loud, don’t you? You would never have heard me laugh!”
“Devi! There was only one time, when that wretched youth Vandiyathevan was speaking with you, that I heard you laugh…”

“Ah! So you even remember that? Very well! If today you hear me laugh out loud, that will be your sign to open the secret door and come in. That will mean the matter is settled. Even now, if you see me laughing at Vandiyathevan, do not be surprised by it…”
“Devi! I think I now understand, at least in part, what your intention is…”
“If you wait a little longer, everything will become clear. If some unexpected obstacle arises, then you will hear my cry of distress. Come at once if you hear that…”
“I shall do as you say, Queen! But I do not wish to hear your cry of distress. I wish only to hear your laughter,” said the magician Ravidasan.

chapters.title: “Alas! A Demon!”
paragraphs: At that very moment, Vandiyathevan, weighed down by a heavy heart, was wandering through the palace’s garden. That garden lay along the outer wall of the palace. The night-blooming flowers had just begun to unfurl their petals. The fragrance of paneer, parijatham, jasmine, mullai, and other blossoms was carried to him by the chilly winds of the month of Aippasi.

“Ah! Should I not be in the gardens of the Pazhaiyarai palace at this hour? And if so, should not the anklets of Princess Kundavai suddenly chime nearby?” his heart mused. “Instead, here I am, trapped in the Kadambur palace! Caught and held captive by a prince possessed by madness!” he thought bitterly.

The way Aditya Karikalan had, for no reason, lashed out at him that evening, and declared, “Never again look upon my face! At dawn tomorrow, I will decide your fate,” had wounded Vandiyathevan’s heart. Never before had the prince been so angry with him. Alas! What use is it to blame him? The prince’s mind had become utterly disturbed. Thinking of his condition, Vandiyathevan felt only pity for him.

That day, Aditya Karikalan’s frenzy had reached its peak. Enthusiasm and exhaustion, rage and exuberance, affection and cruel enmity—each took turns seizing him and tossing him about. In turn, he tossed those around him into similar turmoil. Those nearby never knew, from one moment to the next, what his mood would be, or what he might do.

From sunrise that day, the news that had arrived only served to inflame his madness further. Sambuvaraiyar was the first to come and inform him that Malayaman of Thirukovalur was gathering an army. He expressed his objections and condemnation regarding this.
“Malayaman is an old chieftain. He is over eighty years of age. Why should you fear his coming?” asked the prince.

“Sir! We are descended from the line of Valvil Ori, the lord of Kollimalai. We do not know the meaning of fear. It is only because you are here as a guest that I hesitate. If you alone give your permission…”
“You are ready to set out at once to wage war against the Elder. That is all! Sambuvaraiyar! It was I who sent word, asking my grandfather to come here with his army!”
“For what reason, Prince?”
“Because I have been caught here alone with you, haven’t I? If anything were to happen to me while I am here…”
“Prince! If even the smallest grain of such suspicion exists in your mind, then this very instant—”
“You are about to tell me to leave this place!”

“Sir! This is your kingdom. This is your palace. The tiger flag flies atop its highest tower. Who am I to ask you to leave? If you command, I and my family will leave at once. You may summon Miladudaiyar Malayaman to stay here, and remain fearless in this place.”
“Oh! So, you, born of the valiant lineage of Valvil Ori, are fearless, while I, born of the line of Vijayalaya Chola, am a coward—is that what you are saying?”

“The world knows of the Prince’s diamond heart and heroic courage. At the age of twelve, you entered the battlefield at Sevur and scattered your enemies, earning the name ‘hero of heroes.’ At eighteen, you pursued the returning Veerapandiyan to war, tracked him to his hiding place, and brought back his severed head…”

Hearing this, Aditya Karikalan said, “I know, sir! I know! You all mock me, calling me the tiger who chased down the fleeing foe, the one who brought back the head of the dead Veerapandiyan. I know that the enchantress of Pazhuvoor has spread such rumors about me!”
He laughed with a terrible tone.
Sambuvaraiyar regretted ever having entered into conversation with this furious prince.
“Prince! Whatever I say seems to be misunderstood. Do as you see fit. I shall take my leave.”

“It is well and good that you wish to go and return; but cast aside any thought of leaving this fortress for good. Until I have uncovered the truth behind the conspiracy that took place in this palace four months ago, I too shall not leave this place—and I shall not let you leave either!” declared Aditya Karikalan.
Sambuvaraiyar’s lips trembled. His body shook. Tears brimmed in his eyes.

Parthibendran, who stood nearby, observed this state. “Prince! Just as the Chola clan is famed for its valor, so too is it renowned for its sense of justice. You are not doing justice to this great man. Your words wound his heart. Regarding the meeting of the petty kings that took place here, Sambuvaraiyar has already given a fitting explanation and you yourself have accepted it. Because you have declared that you do not desire the throne, and have refused to go to Thanjavur, the petty kings, thinking of the welfare of the Chola kingdom, deliberated on who should ascend the next rank. If you had agreed to bear the burden of the kingdom, why would they have considered any other course? While the world sings of the valor of Aditya Karikalan, would they ever dream of choosing Madurantaka Deva, who has never even seen a battlefield?”

Aditya Karikalan interrupted, “Yes, yes! As long as I live, it is impossible for another to ascend the Chola throne. That is why they are trying to remove me from their path!” With that, he burst into loud laughter—ha, ha, ha!

“Parthibendra! Did you think I did not know that you too have joined hands with them? Did you think I was unaware that, when Kandamaaran and you accompanied me on that hunt, you were both plotting behind my back? If not for my true friend Vandiyathevan arriving here by fate’s hand, would you not have already sent me to Yama’s world by now?”

Parthibendran glared at Vandiyathevan as though he would kill him with his eyes. “Sir! This traitor has filled your mind with all sorts of poison. If he has convinced you that I have harbored treachery in my heart, then at this very moment—”

“My boy! Who can prove what treachery you have conceived in your heart? Was it not after hearing the words you spoke in answer to my questions, and being bewildered by them, that you went to such lengths to bring me here? Can you deny this?”

“I do not deny it, Prince! Nor is there any need for denial. I am certain that the Lady of Pazhuvoor has intervened in this matter with the best of intentions. Her aim is to bring you here, arrange your marriage with Kandhamaaran’s sister, and thereby ensure that no internal strife arises in the Chola country. There is nothing that would bring us greater joy than to see the radiant crown of the Chola dynasty upon your head. I can bear it if someone finds fault with me, but if anyone dares to slander the Lady of Pazhuvoor, I shall make him taste my sword that very instant!” said Parthibendran, looking at Vandiyathevan, and at the same time, he drew his sword from its scabbard.

“Ah, my valiant friend! Sheathe your sword! When the right time comes, I shall tell you; then you may draw it. Vandiyathevan has not uttered a word against the Lady of Pazhuvoor. He, too, is as confounded as you are. In truth, he swears that the Young Lady of Pazhuvoor is his own sister by birth. He came running all this way just to declare that. Yet, he accuses you of another crime. He claims that you brought my brother from Eezha Nadu in your ship and, on the way, cast him into the sea to drown. What do you say to that?” asked Aditya Karikalan.
At that moment, Kandhamaaran entered, saying, “I shall answer that!”

“Prince! I bring joyous news. The Young Prince did not drown in the sea. Ponniyin Selvan has been hiding all this while in the Choodamani Vihara at Nagapattinam. When the storm raged and the sea surged into the city, he was forced to reveal himself. Surrounded by hundreds of thousands of people, he is now proceeding towards Thanjavur!” Kandhamaaran announced with elation.
He had expected that this news would fill Karikalan with delight, but instead, he was met with bitter disappointment.

Karikalan’s anger now turned in another direction. “What? What did you say? Arulmozhi is heading towards Thanjavur? Surrounded by hundreds of thousands? For what purpose? As a conqueror, is it? What is happening now? Did you not say that he would remain in Nagapattinam until my wishes were known? Then why is he now marching towards Thanjavur?...”
Vandiyathevan interjected, “Sir! The Young Princess said so with certainty. I do not know what reason arose after that. If you wish, I can go and…”

“Aha! You too say you will go? Good, good! All of you have become my enemies. I know all your conspiracies. I know why Arulmozhi is heading towards Thanjavur. It is the scheme of that elder Velar of Kodumbalur. His wish is to tie his younger brother’s daughter around my brother’s neck and seat them both on the Chola throne. I have heard that the Kodumbalur Velar is also marching towards Thanjai with the southern army. My sister, the Young Princess, is also involved in this plot. Yes; you too, of course…”
Vandiyathevan said, “Prince! Forgive me! Neither Ponniyin Selvan nor the Young Princess harbors such intentions. This is the truth; if you wish, I will go and find out the reality myself!”

“Yes, you too say you will go and join in their conspiracy! Kandhamaran! Seize him at once and, if there is any underground prison in this palace, lock him up in it!” As soon as he said this, Kandhamaran approached Vandiyathevan with great enthusiasm.

Immediately, Karikalan changed his command, “No! No! The Chola clan never strays from justice. They will not punish until guilt is certain. Vallavaraiyan! From now on, for the rest of today, do not let your eyes meet mine! That is your punishment! Whether I send you to Thanjai or to prison—I will tell you that tomorrow. Go! Go! Do not stay here another moment! Leave at once!”

At that moment, Vandiyathevan looked at Karikalan’s face. The signal in the corner of his eye seemed to say, “All this is play-acting!” Yet, deciding in an instant that it was best not to remain near the prince, who was in such a state of agitation, Vandiyathevan said, “Sir, your wish is my fortune!” and departed.
Later that afternoon, Vandiyathevan learned that, by the prince’s order, Sambuvarayar and Parthibendran had gone to meet and bring back the Elder of Thirukovalur.
He also learned that the prince and Kandhamaran had conversed privately for a long time.
All these events had left Vandiyathevan deeply dispirited.

What command would the prince give him the next morning? Would he order him to go to Thanjavur? Would he tell him to go to Pazhaiyarai on the way? How wonderful it would be if he did! Vandiyathevan found no joy in life at this Kadambur palace. No one here seemed cheerful. Everyone here always looked as if they had lost something precious. Once darkness fell, this palace no longer seemed like a place where humans lived. It appeared more like a haunted, desolate mansion, inhabited by ghosts and spirits. When and how would he be able to leave this place?...
As Vandiyathevan was lost in these thoughts, a woman's voice suddenly reached his ears, crying out, "Ayyo! A ghost!"

chapters.title: “Go Away!”
paragraphs: Part Five – The Pinnacle of Sacrifice

“Aiyo! A ghost!” cried a voice filled with terror, and Vandiyathevan rushed toward the direction from which it came. Even as he ran, his mind raced: “Isn’t that Manimekalai’s voice? Why has she come here at this hour? What did she see that made her scream so? There can be no such thing as a ghost. Then what could it be? There was real fear in her voice. Will any trouble arise if I approach her now? Her brother is eager to tear me to pieces. Aditya Karikalan is in a frenzy. Who knows what treachery the Queen of Pazhuvoor harbors in her heart?…” Such thoughts flashed rapidly through his mind and vanished. Because of this inner turmoil, he became distracted and careless. Suddenly, the root of a paneer tree caught his foot and he fell to the ground. The end of his upper garment became entangled in the flowering bush beside him.

He tried to compose himself, sat up, and gently attempted to free his garment. What so many enemies and conspirators could not do, this small tree root had accomplished! It had brought him down! Was this an omen of ill fortune? Or was this root restraining him to protect him from danger? Vandiyathevan smiled to himself at the thought.
At that moment, a voice called out, “Amma! Amma! Where are you?” It was Chandramathi’s voice.
“I’m here, dear. I’m near the Alli pond! Come quickly!” replied Manimekalai.

He heard the sound of footsteps, and the sweet tinkling of anklets on their feet. The “Alli pond” Manimekalai referred to was the small marble tank near the ornamental mound in the center of the garden. The pond had been constructed in the shape of an Alli flower. There were a few Alli creepers and red lotus vines in it. At that moment, some flowers floated on its surface. Vandiyathevan had seen this Alli pond before. He must have fallen very close to it! Fortunately, the two women had not noticed him. If it had been daytime and they had seen him fall, they would have burst out laughing and made a mockery of him. Now that Chandramathi had joined Manimekalai, he could slip away unnoticed by the women. In the meantime, the conversation of those women reached his ears.
“Amma! What frightened you? Why did you scream like that?” asked Chandramathi.

“Child! Look at that wall! I saw something upon it. A figure appeared—hair matted atop the head, beard and mustache upon the face. Around its neck—oh, it frightens me even to say it!—there was a garland of skulls! The moment I screamed, it vanished!” said Manimekalai.
“Well and good, Princess! It’s only your mind playing tricks on you! There are no ghosts or demons here! Who could possibly climb and sit atop such a high wall?” said Chandramathi.
“No, girl! My mind does not usually conjure up ghosts or demons…”
“Oh yes! The only face that appears in your dreams and waking thoughts is that of the handsome prince who looks like a god!”
“Shame on you! Even now you make fun of me?”

“Then when should I jest? In the early evening, you come and wait by the lily pond in the flower garden. The scent of jasmine drifts gently through the air… But alas, what happens? While you wait in hope for the Prince of Vallam, a demon with a beard and mustache appears instead!”
“As if it weren’t enough, now you arrive as well!”

“Perhaps it was after seeing me that the demon took fright and fled! Is it not well known throughout the world that ghosts, spirits, and fiends all take to their heels when they see Chandramathi, the maid of Kadambur palace?”
“Chandramathi, enough of your foolish talk for now. Truly, I saw a dreadful figure upon the wall. If you do not believe me, so be it! Tell me, what happened with your errand?”
“My errand did not succeed, Princess!”
“Why? Why?”
“The Prince of Kanchi and the Prince of Kadambur are together, deep in conversation. There is no sign at all of the Prince of Vallam.”
“Perhaps they have sent him off somewhere else?”
“I’m not entirely sure. Your father and the Pallava have gone to confront the Malayaman king. I asked Idumbankari. He said that this evening, Karikalan flew into a rage at Vallatharasan!”
“He’s gone mad, that’s all. He rages at everyone. And then?”
“‘From today, do not show your face to me! Come back after dawn tomorrow!’—he sent him away with those words.”
“Where would he have gone after that?” asked Manimekalai.
“He must be wandering somewhere within these palace walls. That’s why I said—perhaps it was he himself, disguised like a demon, who tried to frighten you.”
“No; I know there are many masqueraders in this palace. But he is not one to deceive others in disguise…”
“This is how women like us, trusting men, end up being deceived.”
“So be it. You go and search again! He must be somewhere within the palace walls, mustn’t he? Tell Idumbankari to look for him as well!”
“Princess! I don’t like that Idumbankari at all, the way he stares and stares. I even feel afraid of him…”
“You’re not afraid of ghosts and demons, but you’re afraid of Idumbankari? Let it be. It’s better not to say anything to him. You go and search once more yourself, and come back!”
“Until then…”
“I’ll stay right here…”
“What if that demon comes here again?…”
“I’ll shout your name and chase it away!”
The soft tinkle of Chandramathi’s anklet signaled her departure.

Vandiyathevan, who had been listening to the conversation, was assailed by a multitude of thoughts. He wondered who the ‘demon’ peering over the wall could have been. He remembered how Alwarkadiyan, disguised as a Kalamukan, had come to his rescue. Perhaps that valiant Vaishnavite himself… Could it be? Has he come from Thanjavur bearing some important message for her? Has he disguised himself so that those here would not recognize him?

Why is Manimekalai so eager to see him? For what reason does she send her friend to search for him and bring him to her? Vandiyathevan had some inkling of Manimekalai’s feelings towards him. That was why he had kept his distance from her. He wished also not to further provoke Kandhamaaran’s enmity. Yet now, she had come to the garden, seated herself alone, and sent for him. Unless it was some matter of great importance, she would not have dared to take such a bold step. Poor girl! Perhaps she too was in some distress. Or perhaps Nandini had sent her with some message. Oh, gods! Here, in this Kadambur palace, every single person seems to be hiding something in their hearts. What Manimekalai said a short while ago was very true. All are wearing masks of deceit. Amidst these people, this innocent girl is caught and struggling. Who knows for what evil purpose the queen of Pazhuvoor has planned to use her? Yes; some suspicion must have arisen in Manimekalai’s mind. She must be anticipating some danger. That is why she seeks his help.

Vandiyathevan recalled the help that guileless, innocent girl had once given him. If she truly was in trouble now and sought his aid, refusing her would be the height of ingratitude. In any case, this was a good opportunity to learn the truth. Chandramathi had gone; Manimekalai was alone. Who would see? He himself might need her help again. If, with her assistance, he could escape from this web of intrigue that had ensnared the palace, it would be for the best. In any case, he could go to her now and learn the truth.

On the marble platform at the edge of the lily pond, Manimekalai was seated. In the sky, shrouded by clouds, a few stars shone here and there; likewise, amidst the thickly spread leaves in the pond, the flowers lifted their heads. In the surrounding darkness, the whiteness of those night-blooming flowers stood out vividly. Beyond the lily pond, in the jasmine thickets, half-bloomed flowers and buds glimmered like pearls set in a blue canopy.

As Manimekalai was watching this, she suddenly heard footsteps behind her and, startled, turned around. Seeing a figure approaching very close, she hurriedly tried to stand up, but her foot slipped and she nearly fell into the pond behind her.
“Princess! It’s me!” said Vandiyathevan, rushing forward and catching Manimekalai to steady her.

A shiver ran through Manimekalai’s body. Embarrassed by the suddenness of the situation, she tried to push his hands away and free herself. But at that moment, her arms lacked the strength for it! In the attempt, she almost lost her balance again and swayed backward.
Vandiyathevan held her more firmly, supporting her and bringing her safely to the front.
With a great effort, Manimekalai composed herself and said in an angry voice, “Let go! Do not touch me!”
Vandiyathevan released her at once. “Princess! Forgive me!” he said.
Still trembling, her voice quivering, Manimekalai asked, “Why should I forgive you?”
“For startling you by coming upon you so suddenly, that’s all!”
“You came, that’s one thing! But why did you have to touch me and hold me?” Manimekalai’s tone showed she had regained her composure.
“I only caught you to keep you from falling into the pond!”

“How wonderful! The other day, when I fell into the lake and was struggling in the water, you didn’t show such concern! But now, you rush to save me from falling into this pond that barely reaches my knees?”
“That was my fault!”
“You have done nothing wrong; all the fault is mine.”
“How is that? You have done nothing wrong. You are saying this out of some anger toward me!”
“The other day, you suddenly entered the room where I was, from inside the hunting lodge. Even then, you startled me. I should have screamed and handed you over to my father right then!”
“That day, you saved me from great danger. I shall never forget it.”
“In return, I shall never forget the manner in which you expressed your gratitude. Never have I seen anyone as ungrateful as you…”
“Princess! This is a grave accusation! In what way am I ungrateful? Tell me!”
“You lied, saying that murderers were pursuing you. While I went to the hunting pavilion to see for myself, you ran off like a thief, without even telling me!”
“You say I ran off like a thief?”
“It is wrong to say ‘like a thief’; you were a thief indeed!”
“Princess, you do not know how desperate my situation was that day…”
“For those who do not know, you could have explained, couldn’t you? Who stopped you from doing so?”
“Your friend Chandramathi did. As soon as you entered the hunting pavilion, Chandramathi came in through another entrance. To avoid being seen by her, I hid in the music chamber.”
“And then you vanished from there as if by magic!”

“No; I climbed up the ladder, crossed over the terraces, and leapt down from the fortress wall. Princess! If anyone had discovered me that day, the mission I had undertaken would have been ruined; and you too would have been subjected to ridicule…”
“How much concern you have for this foolish girl!”
“It is true, I am concerned!”
“If that is so, you have been back here for so many days now, haven’t you? Could you not have explained the reason for your sudden flight, instead of remaining silent?”
“I was only waiting for the right opportunity…”
“Why, sir, are these mere words? You never even turn to look in the direction where I am!”
“Sister!…”
“I am not your sister!”
“You are the sister of my friend Kandhamaaran; therefore, you are my sister as well.”
“Kandhamaaran is not my brother; nor is he your friend. He is a cruel enemy to both of us…”

“Princess! At least you know that much! Until a few days ago, Kandhamaaran was my dearest friend. Now, he has changed completely. Parthibendran is waiting for a chance to put a noose around my neck. Aditya Karikalan’s moods shift from moment to moment—one instant he speaks with affection, the next he flares up in anger. I spend my days expecting danger at every turn. In such a situation, if I have come seeking you only to express my gratitude…”
“Sir! I am very glad to see how eager you are to save yourself…”
“Princess, I am not worried about myself. I am not concerned for my own life. I am only anxious that no harm should come to you because of me.”
“You are melting away in worry. Chandramathi used to say all men are deceivers. Now I am certain it is true.”
“Let anyone say what they will. As long as I live, I will never forget you! Nor will I forget the help you have given me!”
Manimekalai fell into a brief silence, lost in thought, and then said, “Sir, will you say once more what you just said?”
“I will say it a thousand times if you wish. As long as I live, I will never forget the help you have given me!” Vandiyathevan declared firmly.
“What use is it to say it a thousand times? Should you not try to fulfill it as well?”
“In what way should I try? Tell me, Princess!”
“You will be grateful to me only as long as you are alive? Therefore, you must first save your life. If not for your sake, then for mine—save yourself!”
“Princess! What is this?…”
“Sir! Tell me the truth! Were you listening to the conversation my friend and I were having just now?”
“Forgive me, Princess! I heard you cry out, ‘Oh, a ghost!’ and rushed here. By then, your friend Chandramathi had already arrived. It so happened that I overheard your conversation.”
“You know, don’t you, that I sent her to search for you and bring you here?”
“I heard it with my own ears. That is why I came to you…”
“Otherwise, you wouldn’t have come near me at all. Ah, what consideration! Let it be. No matter how stone-hearted you may be, my heart cannot bear it. If you are in danger, I cannot remain silent.”
“Princess! I am well aware of the perilous situation I am in. Is there some new danger approaching that I do not know of?”
“Sir! Leave this palace at once!”
“You are asking me to flee in secret?”
“One must not flee the battlefield. But what is wrong in escaping from traitors?”
“Who are these traitors?”
“Who else? Kandhamaaran and Parthibendran.”
“I cannot run away from this palace out of fear of them.”
“I cannot bear it, knowing that harm may befall you because of my brother.”
“Princess! How can you be responsible for Kandhamaaran’s actions?”
“It is because of me that he and Parthibendran are plotting to harm you.”
“If I suffer for your sake, that is my good fortune. I will consider it a repayment for the help you have given me…”
“Nandini Devi was right!”
“Ah! What did the Queen of Pazhuvoor say to you?”

“If I told you to save your life, you would not listen. I must try some other means,” she said. “Sir! Please, I beg you, come with me. The Lady of Pazhuvoor wishes to see you at once on some urgent matter.”
“You know what this urgent matter is, don’t you?”
“I do; there is news that when the Periya Pazhuvettaraiyar was crossing the Kollidam, his boat capsized…”
“I have heard that too!”
“You must go at once and find out the truth about it. The Lady of Pazhuvoor is going to ask you for this in person.”
Vandiyathevan paused for a moment in thought, then asked, “Didn’t the Lady of Pazhuvoor warn you not to tell me any of this beforehand?”
“Yes, she did!”
“Then why did you tell me?”

“It is because my mind is troubled, sir. Until a few days ago, I was a woman who knew nothing of deceit or cunning. I never suspected anyone. Even if my friends spoke ill of someone, I would not believe it. Now, I suspect everyone; I doubt everything.”
“It seems my waking gaze has brought misfortune upon you.”

“In a way, that is true! The younger Lady of Pazhuvoor sent me to bring you to her. While speaking with her, I felt not the least suspicion. Everything seemed right… But once I left her, doubts about her began to arise.”
“What suspicion, Princess? What doubt do you have about Nandini Devi?”
“I wonder if she too is plotting harm against you.”
“Why has this suspicion come to you? What harm could she do to me?”
“That, I cannot say. But if I think over her words and actions, they fill me with doubt. Often, she holds a long sword in her hand and speaks of strange things.”
“I do not fear a sword in a woman’s hand. More than that…”

“You fear the swords that are like eyes upon a face. That is the tale everyone tells, sir. But I am not warning you to be afraid of Nandini Devi’s sword alone. Recall, if you will, the very first time you came from the hunting pavilion into the room where I was staying…”
“I remember it well…”

“You said that some murderers had followed you. At first, I did not believe it. Afterwards, I went into the hunting pavilion to see for myself. Behind the animals there, it seemed as if some people were hiding. I could not determine then whether they had come to kill you, or whether they had come along with you. If I were to speak about them, I would also have to speak about you, would I not?”
“Only now do I truly realize how great a help you have been to me.”

“I am not mentioning that matter now for that reason. Just a short while ago, Nandini Devi sent me to bring you to her. Immediately, I turned back as if to ask her something. She had locked the door. From inside, faint voices from the hunting pavilion could be heard. Sir! Let me share my suspicion with you now. It seems that some people have come and are hiding in the hunting pavilion. I also suspect that there must be some connection between them and the Lady of Pazhuvoor.”

Only now did Vandiyathevan fully grasp the gravity of the situation. His inner sense had been warning him all along that some dire event was about to take place today. The news Manimekalai had shared only confirmed his fears.
“Princess! I need you to do me a favor!”
“Tell me what it is!”

“There is a way that leads from outside the hunting pavilion through an underground passage. Now, there is a door through the room where Nandini Devi is staying. Besides these, is there not a third way?”
“Yes; there is a path used by the servants. Whenever new guests come to the palace, my father usually takes them in through that way…”
“Princess! Take me to the hunting pavilion through that way at once!”
“For what reason?”
“To find out who are those hiding there, and with what intention they have come…”
“I came to save you from danger. Now you are asking to walk straight into it.”
“There is always a dagger at my waist, Princess! It is easier to face a known danger than an unknown one. And better still if we walk into it prepared.”
“If you agree to one condition, I will take you to the hunting pavilion.”
“What is that?”
“I too will come with you; I also have a small dagger at my waist!” said Manimekalai, showing her dagger.
Vandiyathevan agreed to this.
“In that case, follow me quickly. We must leave before Chandramathi comes here looking for me,” she said.

Manimekalai led Vandiyathevan across the garden. Then, she guided him along the shadowed edges of the palace walls, where the darkness was thick. Next, she brought him inside the palace, through deserted corridors and passageways where no one was about. Finally, she stopped near a doorway that was firmly shut. She made Vandiyathevan wait there, hurried away, and returned with a hand-lamp. She opened the door and, holding the lamp aloft, revealed a narrow staircase descending before them.
Both of them went down the steps. After a short while, Manimekalai, who was walking ahead, suddenly stopped and, in a soft voice, said, “Wait! Doesn’t it sound like footsteps? Do you hear it too?”

chapters.title: The Monkey’s Trap!
paragraphs: Vandiyathevan listened carefully, his ears alert. For a moment, it seemed as if he could hear the sound of footsteps. Suddenly, the sound stopped. Then, it was heard again. Now, the sound seemed to be receding, growing fainter as it moved away.
“Sir! Must we really go further up? Wouldn’t it be better to turn back?” asked Manimekalai.
“Princess! It is not my habit to turn back once I have set my foot forward!” replied Vallavarayan.
“If you wish, you may call it a monkey’s grip!” she said.
“Didn’t your friend Chandramathi once describe me as ‘monkey-face’? Wouldn’t the grip suit the face?” he retorted.
Exchanging such words, Vandiyathevan, who had until then been following behind Manimekalai, now tried to overtake her and go ahead. Manimekalai tried to prevent him.

The two jostled against each other. The lamp in Manimekalai’s hand slipped and fell with a thud. It rolled down two or three steps with a clatter and went out. Darkness engulfed that uneven, sloping pathway.
“Princess! What have you done?” exclaimed Vallavarayan.
“Why did you try to overtake me and go ahead?” asked Manimekalai.
“It is not my habit to let women go ahead when danger is near!” said Vandiyathevan.
“It would be good if you clearly told me what your habits are and what they are not. I shall conduct myself accordingly.”
“Very well, my lady! I shall tell you when there is time.”
“What is lacking in time now? Come, let us turn back to the garden. There, we can sit and you may tell me at leisure.”
“If you are afraid to walk in the dark, you may turn back!...” “When a brave warrior like you is by my side, what have I to fear?”
“Then come along, let us go! What use is there in standing here on the path?”
So saying, Vandiyathevan tried to walk ahead, but his foot slipped and he nearly fell. Manimekalai caught hold of him, preventing his fall.

“Sir! There are many rises and dips along this path. In this darkness, it’s impossible to tell where the steps are, or where the level ground lies. I have walked this way countless times. I know well where the steps and turns are. So, no matter how valiant and daring you may be, it is best if you take my hand and follow behind me. Otherwise, you will never reach the hunting lodge. You’ll trip and fall somewhere along the way!” said Manimekalai.
“Princess! I shall walk as you command. My respects!” replied Vandiyathevan.

In the darkness, Manimekalai took hold of one of Vallavaraiyan’s hands. She noticed that Vandiyathevan’s hand was trembling. ‘He fears neither enemies nor conspirators; why then does he seem afraid to hold the hand of this foolish girl?’ she wondered to herself.
For a while, the two walked on in silence. Vandiyathevan stumbled often, nearly falling each time. Each time, Manimekalai had to grip his hand more tightly to keep him from falling.
“The road to hell must be just as dark as this!” said Vandiyathevan.
“Oh! Have you already been to hell and returned?” Manimekalai asked.
“I have never been to hell, nor to heaven. That’s what the elders say!”
“Their elders must have told them so!”
Vandiyathevan pondered how this girl, who until recently would have been shy even to come before four people, had now become so bold and outspoken.
“If the road to hell is dark, how must the road to heaven be?” asked Manimekalai.
“They say it is filled with a single, all-pervading radiance; that it blazes with the brilliance of a million suns!”
“If that is so, then I would prefer the path that leads to hell! Even a single sun dazzles my eyes. The light of a million suns would surely blind me!” said Manimekalai.
“If you take the path that leads to hell, won’t you end up in hell in the end?” asked Vallavarayan.
“If I follow a heroic man like you, perhaps even the road to hell might lead to heaven!” replied Manimekalai.
“If I could take the hand of a princess like you and walk, even hell itself would become heaven!” said Vandiyathevan.
At once, he bit his lip in regret. “What have I said? What if this maiden misunderstands my words?” he worried.
“Seeing how your hand is trembling, it does not seem like you are on your way to heaven. Your whole body is shaking as if you are heading to a battlefield!” said Manimekalai.
“Princess! Who knows if, at the end of this journey, a battlefield awaits me?”
“You are the one who insists on never turning back once you set your foot forward, aren’t you? Who knows how many murderers are lurking in the hunting pavilion?”
“Let there be as many as they wish; I am not afraid of them. What I am thinking about is—if Kandhamaaran were to see you and me walking hand in hand through the darkness like this…”
“Oh no! As long as I live, my brother will never harm you. Half of what I saw in my dream has already come true; perhaps the other half may become reality as well. Who can say?” said Manimekalai.
At that moment, hearing the sound of a door being bolted somewhere, both of them started and stood still.
“We are very close to the hunting pavilion now!” whispered Manimekalai in a soft voice.

By now, a little distance ahead, a faint light became visible. Gradually, the light grew brighter and seemed to be approaching them. Manimekalai let go of Vandiyathevan’s hand and stepped slightly aside.
In the next moment, Idumbankari appeared before them—one hand holding aloft a lamp, the other gripping a twisted, intricately wrought, sharp dagger.
Upon seeing them, he stood as if struck dumb with astonishment. But both Manimekalai and Vandiyathevan could tell that he was merely pretending.
“Amma, Ayya! What is this? Why are you wandering alone in the darkness like this? If you had told your servant, wouldn’t I have come carrying a lamp? Where are you headed?” he asked.

“Idumbankari! Haven’t you heard the news that Malayaman is marching with his army? That’s why I set out with the young prince of Vallam, to check whether all the gates and secret tunnels of the fort are securely locked,” replied Manimekalai.
“Astonishing, mother! That’s exactly what I was doing too!” said Idumbankari.
“I thought as much. The lamp we brought with us went out when it fell along the way. We saw a glimmer of light here and guessed it must be you, so we came up.”
“The young master asked me to check, so I went and looked. All the secret passages are properly sealed and locked. Shall we go back now, mother?”
“Give me the lamp in your hand and you may go! This prince needs to fetch a spear from the hunting hall—his own spear has gone missing. What if war breaks out at any moment?”
“Yes, Ammayi! War could break out at any time. So it’s best not to take strangers into the hunting hall. I needn’t tell you what you already know.”

“That’s true, Kari! But he is no stranger. He is the dearest friend of the young master—his very life! Even if some new relationship is to be forged, let it be so. Hand over the lamp and go!” said Manimekalai.
Idumbankari, with a look of distaste, handed the lamp to the princess and departed.
Vandiyathevan and Manimekalai walked onward, approaching the hunting pavilion. From somewhere nearby, the cry of an owl echoed.
“What is this? How did an owl come inside the palace?” Manimekalai exclaimed in astonishment.

“Perhaps the dead owl inside the hunting pavilion has come back to life—who knows? Was it not that, once upon a time, even a dead monkey sprang to life at the sight of the princess?” Vandiyathevan replied.
The door to the hunting pavilion was locked from the outside. Manimekalai took the key she had brought, inserted it, and opened the lock. Then, she gently pushed the door open.
The two of them entered. At first, all they could see around them were the terrifying forms of dead elephants, bears, tigers, deer, crocodiles, hawks, and owls.
When they lifted the lamp and peered more closely, they noticed that behind those beasts—half hidden, half revealed—sat several human figures.
At that moment, the door through which they had entered slammed shut with a loud bang.

Vandiyathevan turned to see who had closed the door with such force. In that very instant, he was seized from behind and thrust forward violently. He collided headlong with the very monkey whose tail he had once hidden behind.
Two strong arms gripped him tightly. Only then did he truly, through painful experience, understand the strength of a “monkey’s grip.”
His attempt to draw the dagger from his waist was futile. He could not turn this way or that.
The monkey’s hands—or perhaps two human hands joining with the monkey’s—held him fast with unyielding strength.
Two more hands deftly unfastened the dagger from his waist and took it.
“Aiyo!” Manimekalai screamed in terror, rushing toward him. The dagger was extended menacingly toward her chest.

“Do not make a sound. If you remain quiet for a little while—if you listen to what we say—there will be no danger to either of your lives. But if you raise your voices, both of you will lose your lives. First, this overly talkative young man will fall dead!” said a voice.
Vandiyathevan recognized it as the voice of Ravidasan.
“Princess! Please remain calm for a moment! Let us listen to what they have come for, and what they have to say. We can find out their intentions,” said Vandiyathevan.

chapters.title: The Pandya Queen
paragraphs: Those who had tied Vandiyathevan to the tailless monkey now bound Manimekalai near him, fastening her to the antlers of a stag mounted on the wall.
“Sorcerer! I am your enemy—why do you bind the Princess of Kadambur? Let her go!” cried Vandiyathevan.
Ravidasan looked at him and said, “Patience, brother, patience! Many times you have interfered in our affairs. Each time, we have spared your life. Yet you have not ceased to follow us!”
Vandiyathevan laughed.
“What is so amusing? Does the embrace of a tailless monkey delight you so much?” asked Ravidasan.
“No! I was only laughing at what you just said,” replied Vallavarayan.
“And what, in what I said, makes you laugh so?”

“You said that I keep following you. Could it not be said that you are the ones who keep following me? That you are the ones interfering in my business? Look now! I was taking the Princess of Kadambur with me on an important mission. You interfered and tied me up with this monkey!”

“Oh! Is that the truth of it? Very well, then. Consider that we are the ones interfering in your affairs. But let me tell you—this will be the last time such a thing happens. If you escape with your life today, you will never see us again!”
“In that case, I must do my best to stay alive! Sorcerer! Teach me a trick so that I might escape with my life!” said Vandiyathevan.
“I shall indeed teach you. Whatever happens in this hall, or in the next room, just watch quietly! Do not act rashly! Your life will not be in danger.”
“Why do you have such affection for me? Why do you let me live instead of killing me?”
“Listen to that! Yes, it is utter foolishness! But it is the command of our Devi!”
“Who is your Devi?”
“Do you still not know? It is Pandimadevi. The heroic consort of the Pandya Emperor, Nandini Devi, who now resides in the house of Periya Pazhuvetaraiyar!”
“A fine heroic consort, indeed!”
“Shame on you! You wicked boy! If you utter a single word against our Devi, you will lose your life! Beware!”
“Is it not you who are slandering the Queen of Pazhuvur? You call a woman who lives in another man’s house the consort of Veerapandiyan?”
“So what? Was not Sita, the wife of Rama, for a time in the house of Ravana?”
“But Rama went and brought back Sita Devi, did he not?”
“We too have come to take back our Pandima Devi. Whatever reason she had for imprisoning herself in the palace at Pazhuvur, that ends today…”
“Ah! And what is that reason?”
“Wait a little while with patience! You will know for yourself. If you show your wickedness, not only you, but this woman too will meet a terrible fate!”
Saying this, Ravidasan made to move toward the opposite wall.
“Magician! Tell me just one more thing before you go!” said Vandiyathevan.
Ravidasan turned and said, “Young man! Do not call me ‘magician’ again!”
“Then, how should I address you?”
“You must address me respectfully as the Chief Minister!”
“Sir! Of which great kingdom are you the Chief Minister?”
“Do you not know? Of the Pandya Mahasamrajyam! Did you not witness the coronation ceremony held near the Pallipadai?”
“I did witness it. But I thought it was some delusion of my mind…”
“Is that why you haven’t spoken of it to anyone?”
“I told a couple of people; they called me a madman. They said I must have had some dreadful nightmare…”
“Ah! Let them go on thinking that way. Even we spared your life only because we were sure no one would believe you if you spoke of it outside!”
“Sorcerer! Is that the only reason you let me live?”
“What else?”
“Didn’t your queen intercede on my behalf?”
“So what if she did?”
“Even now, I can count on her recommendation.”
“Wait until you receive it!”
“Sorcerer, your queen sent this Kadambur princess to summon me here in haste. That’s why the two of us have come together…”
“My lord! There are other ways to reach the queen’s chambers! Why would you come by this path?”
“I don’t need to explain that to you. If the queen asks, I will tell her…”
“Wait until the queen comes and asks you herself!”
“Sorcerer! Tell them to untie me and the daughter of Sambuvarayar at once! Otherwise…”
“What will you do?”
“I will shout so loudly that this hall will tremble!”
“The moment you raise your voice, three spears will strike you at once—beware!”
Vandiyathevan looked around keenly.
Yes; three conspirators stood ready, each with a spear in hand.

“Thambi! You are a very cunning fellow. There was a time when I even wished to have you join us. But you have fallen into the snare of that Pazhayarai enchantress. Let that be. Now, act wisely! If you make a sound, your death is certain!” Thus warning him, Ravidasan turned toward the elephant’s head that was fixed to the opposite wall. For a moment, he pressed his ear to the wall and listened. Then, grasping the long tusks of the elephant, he twisted them. A small opening appeared. The bright light of the lamps burning in the inner chamber streamed through, illuminating the hunting hall with a silvery glow, like the full moon’s beams.
Vandiyathevan turned to the side and saw that Princess Manimekalai had taken the small knife tucked at her waist and cut through the ropes that bound her.

The small lamp Manimekalai had taken from Idumbankari burned with a faint, flickering light in one corner of the hunting hall. Its glow did not fall upon Manimekalai. Moreover, since the conspirators were all focused on Vandiyathevan, none paid any attention to the Kadambur princess. Vandiyathevan noticed that Manimekalai had freed herself from her bonds. At once, he pursed his lips and let out a cry like an owl.

At first, the three conspirators stood startled. Ravidasan, who was peering through the open aperture, turned around in alarm. “Ah! Is that your doing?” he exclaimed, and rushed toward Vandiyathevan. The moment he took his hands off the elephant’s tusks, the opening in the wall closed. Darkness once again enveloped the hunting hall. All three conspirators, weapons in hand, rushed toward Vandiyathevan.

Suddenly, a stag with long, twisted antlers charged at one of them; a gigantic bear leapt upon another, knocking him to the ground; and upon the third, a crocodile with gaping jaws and fearsome teeth sprang forth. Upon Ravidasan’s head, a huge, monstrous bat swooped down with a thud.

Stunned by these sudden attacks, the conspirators stood motionless for a moment. In that instant, Manimekalai approached Vandiyathevan and cut his bonds. Freed, Vandiyathevan seized the tailless monkey that had been clinging to him and hurled it at the conspirators. All four of them, struck by these unexpected... They pushed aside the bodies of the dead beasts and slowly managed to rise to their feet. By this time, Vandiyathevan had picked up a spear in his hand. He stood ready, prepared to turn back any attackers who might come at them.
At that very moment, the door to Nandini Devi’s bedchamber opened wide. Light streamed into the hunting pavilion, illuminating everything with a sudden brilliance.
The next instant, Nandini herself entered the hunting pavilion. “Sorcerer! What is this madness? What commotion are you causing here?” she demanded as she strode forward.

chapters.title: The Iron Heart Softened!
paragraphs: Nandini was momentarily startled upon seeing Vandiyathevan and Manimekalai inside the hunting pavilion.
“Oh! How did you come here?” she asked.
“Devi! I came because your friend said it was your command. Only after arriving here did I realize that one should not heed a woman’s counsel,” replied Vandiyathevan.
“Sister! I did not give him advice; I merely begged him to come with me to see you!” said Manimekalai.
Nandini quickly mastered her initial surprise and smiled.
“My dear friend! When we women beseech men, it is as good as giving them advice!” she said.

“Is it only like giving advice? Say rather, Devi, that it is like issuing a command! Saying you had summoned me, the princess here seized me by the hand and dragged me along. The result is that I have now fallen into the clutches of these murderers!” said Vandiyathevan.
“Sir! From what I see here, it does not appear that they are murderers. If I had not come here just now, it seems you would have slain them all yourself!” said Nandini.
“Sister! They are murderers indeed! Just a short while ago, they tied him up together with that tailless monkey!...”
Nandini, with a gentle laugh, said, “Manimekalai! Did you not once say that he hid behind that tailless monkey? Somehow, they seem to have found out about it!”

“Not ‘somehow,’ sister! The very men I told you I saw in this hunting pavilion the day before you arrived—these are they! That day itself they chased after him. Luckily, he escaped from their hands and ran away!...” “Why have you brought him here again today, Manimekalai? For what reason did you lead him along this path?”

“Sister! Just a short while ago, my brother Kandhamaaran said he was going to see you. I brought him this way so that he would not be seen by my brother; it turned out to be for the best. Otherwise, these murderers…”

“Sister! They are not murderers. They have not come to kill him. Two or three times now, he has fallen into their hands alone, yet they have spared his life. You can ask him yourself and learn the truth.”
“If that is so, who are they, sister? Is what they said earlier true? Are they known to you? Have they come to take you away?” Manimekalai asked in astonishment.
“Yes, friend! They have come to rescue me and take me away. I will explain everything in detail. Both of you, come with me to the next room! Let them remain here!” said Nandini.

Then, turning to Ravidasan, she said, “Sorcerer! If you harm either of these two in any way, I will consider it as harm done to me. Wherever and in whatever situation you may meet them in the future, you must treat them with the utmost respect!”
Ravidasan replied, “Devi! Forgive me. This youth knows our secret signal. It was he who gave the owl’s call just now!”

“From that itself, could you not tell that this brave man is one of us? Sorcerer! Where has your sharp wit gone? Let bygones be bygones. From now on, until I give further instructions, not a sound must be heard here! Be careful!” said Nandini.
Then, Nandini, Manimekalai, and Vandiyathevan entered Nandini’s chamber through the elephant-faced entrance. The door was immediately closed behind them.

“Sister! You are very clever! It was wise of you to bring him through the hunting pavilion. Your brother has just left from here. He said he was going to bring Aditya Karikalan. I must send you away before he returns. I must also bid you farewell!” said Nandini.
“Akka! What is this? Didn’t you say you were sending him to learn the truth about your husband? But now you say you are bidding him farewell?” asked Manimekalai.

“After speaking with your brother, I have changed my mind, dear sister! Whether Pazhuvetaraiyar is alive or not, I can no longer remain here. And it is dangerous for this brave man to stay here any longer, sir! You must leave this place at once. Even if you do not care for your own life, at least for the sake of this woman, leave immediately!” said Nandini.
“Akka! If he is going, ask him to take me with him. After you and he are gone, I cannot bear to remain imprisoned in this palace!” said Manimekalai.

“Princess! You have not understood the mind of the Queen of Pazhuvur. She says that if she leaves this place, you may marry Aditya Karikalan and become the Empress of the Thanjai Empire!” said Vallavaraiyan.

“No, I did not say that. I do not wish for any woman to have the misfortune of marrying Aditya Karikalan. Least of all, should that fate befall Manimekalai, who is dearer to me than my own life. Sir! You are twisting my words to suit your will. If you escape now, perhaps one day you may have the fortune to take this woman’s hand in marriage! Manimekalai! If your love for him is true, urge him to leave this place at once!” said Nandini.
“Rani! I am ready to go. But I beg one thing from you. If you give it to me, I will leave immediately!” said Vandiyathevan.
“Sir! What is there in my possession that you would ask for? Tell me!”
“There is a sword with the fish emblem in your keeping. If you give it to me, I will leave. You know that I lost my own sword in the Kollidam river, do you not?” said Vandiyathevan.

“Sir! There are plenty of swords and spears in the hunting pavilion. You may take whichever you wish and depart this very moment. Why do you ask for the only weapon a woman like me has kept to protect her own life?”
“Devi, is it only to protect your own life that you perform puja to that sword? Tell me the truth!”
“I keep that dagger not only to protect my life, but to safeguard a chastity dearer to me than life itself.”
“Devi! Is there no other purpose?”
“What other purpose could I possibly have?”
“It could also be to exact vengeance for the death of Veera Pandiyan, could it not?”

“I thought you would not bring up that subject while Manimekalai is present. Now, there is no longer any need for me to hide it. Sister! You too must know. Understand well the reason I have come to this Kadambur palace!”
So saying, Nandini Devi took up the sword marked with the fish emblem, which lay beside her on the bed.

“I have not come here to quell the internal strife of the Chola Empire. Nor have I come to divide the kingdom between Madhurantaka Devar and Aditya Karikalan. I have not come to the Kadambur palace to feast and revel! Sister! I have not come to arrange your marriage either. I have come only to exact vengeance upon the villain who severed the head of Veera Pandiyan. This is the sword of the Pandya clan! Upon this sword I have sworn an oath. I have come to fulfill that oath. Tonight, I shall either fulfill my vow, or I shall end my own life!” Nandini spoke thus, her voice trembling with passion, and fell silent.
“Is it because you fear I will stand in your way that you ask me to leave? Are you trying to frighten me with threats to my life?” asked Vandiyathevan.
“Ah! So you intend to thwart my vengeance? Very well! Who has forbidden you? Is it not your plan to go to your friend and tell him all this, and thus prevent him from coming here?”
“Devi, I have come to you because I know I cannot stop him by telling him. I have come to fall at your feet and beg you, to plead with you not to commit this sinful deed…”
